lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The dated experience roles are not in reverse-chronological order.
items.because: Harbor Payments (2024) appears after Crestline Logistics (through 2023), making the timeline harder to follow.

items.says: Consider whether experience should lead instead of education if the MBA is not relevant to the target role.
The mix of operations, mechanical, and product experience may leave readers unsure of the target direction.
items.because: The resume presents a substantial operations background, a recent mechanical role, and product experience from an internship and student venture.

items.says: Replace the placeholder-looking phone number and profile URL if they appear on the submitted resume.
items.because: Submitted contact details should be working contact information.

items.says: Clarify the period or number of jobs behind the under-five-days result.
items.because: That would help readers understand what the metric measures.

items.says: Clarify whether the dry-dock result reflects your work alone or the team's.
items.because: That would show your share of the result.

items.says: Add a verifiable outcome or a specific scope of records, if available.
items.because: The outcome is less clear than in the other bullets.

items.says: Clarify your relationship to the harbor authority if the employer context does not make it obvious.
Explain what you did with the scorecards or how they informed decisions.
items.because: The bullet is mainly a responsibility statement and is less persuasive than bullets showing a measurable result.

items.says: Add the timeframe for the 30% reduction, if available.
Ensure the pick-error metric is comparable across both sites.
Clarify the periods compared by the 18% and 11% forecast-error figures.
items.because: That would help a reader interpret the result.

items.says: Clarify how forecast error was calculated.
items.because: That would help a reader interpret the result.

items.says: Keep the consensus forecasting change distinct from the resulting error reduction.
Clarify which parts of the rollout, procedures, training, and negotiations you personally led or owned.
items.because: The bullet combines several activities and makes the central contribution hard to see.

items.says: Explain how the 1,800 driver hours were measured or attributed.
Shorten or refocus the bullet.
items.because: Its current length makes the central contribution harder to see.

items.says: Clarify how the 2,300 merchants relate to the before-and-after measurement.
items.because: It is unclear whether both figures apply to the same pilot cohort or period.

items.says: Clarify the verification change's scope.
items.because: The description should not imply a broader change to verification requirements than actually occurred.

items.says: Describe the change from 61% to 66% as a percentage-point increase.
items.because: The increase is five percentage points, not just a numerical lift.

items.says: The checkout test and result are repeated in the later A/B-test bullet.
items.because: The retained bullets should demonstrate different contributions.

items.says: Clarify how shipping the change to all merchants relates to the later regional rollout.
items.because: It is unclear whether these were separate releases, regions, or stages.

items.says: Clarify whether support tickets closed was an adapted proxy for RICE Reach and what was actually scored.
items.because: Support tickets closed may not be the usual meaning of that RICE factor.

items.says: Clarify your individual contribution and the decision the research and analysis informed.
items.because: The bullet lists several steps, but its outcome is not distinct from the following roadmap presentation.

items.says: Distinguish this analysis from the following roadmap presentation.
items.because: Their outcomes overlap.

items.says: The checkout A/B test and conversion result duplicate the earlier checkout bullet.
items.because: The evidence should be combined or limited to detail that adds something distinct.

items.says: The session-level test is presented as an effect on merchants' customers.
items.because: Session-level randomization supports the measured session-level conversion outcome, not a direct measurement of broader merchant impact.

items.says: Clarify how the funded regional rollout relates to the earlier claim that the checkout flow shipped to all merchants.
Distinguish the onboarding results from the follow-up roadmap if they were separate initiatives.
Distinguish the students the app was launched to from those who actually used it.
items.because: The launch figure and the following weekly-active-user figure describe different things.

items.says: Confirm that the 9 tonnes were actually redistributed.
Confirm that the food-redistribution measurement period was the stated first year.
The 150% weekly-active-user increase is calculated incorrectly.
items.because: Rising from 400 to 1,150 is a 187.5% increase.

items.says: Clarify the timing and connection between the 60 interviews and the pickup reminders.
The change from 75% to 95% is labeled as a 20% increase rather than a 20-percentage-point increase.
Add the measurement period or denominator for the fill rate, if useful.
items.because: That would help explain how the rate was calculated.

items.says: Make explicit that the $2.4M annual saving was modeled, not realized.
items.because: Funding a pilot does not establish that the projected saving was achieved.

items.says: The pilot-funding outcome is repeated in the final practicum bullet.
items.because: Both bullets use the same pilot decision unless they show different contributions.

items.says: Make clear who mapped intake and shortened the form, including your contribution as team lead.
items.because: The passive construction obscures who did the work.

items.says: Distinguish adopted changes from changes that were merely recommended.
The pilot approval repeats the outcome in the first practicum bullet.
items.because: Both bullets use the same outcome unless they show clearly different contributions.

items.says: Support “requirements writing” elsewhere in the resume or reconsider listing it.
items.because: That skill is not clearly demonstrated elsewhere.

items.says: Consider adding relevant tools you have used for the target role.
items.because: The current list may be too narrow for some target roles.
